title: Real-time fraud scoring pods evicted unexpectedly
reported_symptoms: Our real-time transaction scoring service dropped from twenty replicas down to two. Latency spiked and transactions started failing downstream.
investigation: Executed kubectl describe node worker-compute-07. Observed DiskPressure condition active. Checked disk usage:du -sh /var/lib/docker/* revealed massive build caches and stale container images taking up 180GB.
root_cause: Continuous CI/CD deployments over the weekend left behind numerous dangling images that filled the node disk.
resolution: Triggered manual docker system prune, cleared evicted pods, and set up a cron job to clean up unused images weekly.

title: Persistent storage detachment failure halting llama training pod
reported_symptoms: Our heavy fine-tuning job for the 70B parameter model is stuck at ContainerCreating. We suspect the PVC ran out of inode space or storage quota limits were hit on the primary network volume.
investigation: Checked the pod status via kubectl describe pod llm-trainer-node-3. Observed event warnings: Warning FailedAttachVolume Attach volume "pvc-9a8b7c6d" to node "gpu-worker-12" failed: Volume is already exclusively attached to node "gpu-worker-08" and can't be detached.
root_cause: ReadWriteOnce volume was orphaned on a previous node during an unexpected hypervisor crash.
resolution: Forcibly detached the persistent volume from gpu-worker-08 using the cloud block storage CLI and restarted the scheduler queue.

title: Vector search API failing readiness checks intermittently
reported_symptoms: The vector database cluster is flapping. Pods alternate between ready and unready states every few minutes. Queries take forever to return even though index memory usage is stable.
investigation: Examined kubelet logs and discovered liveness probe timeouts. Ran top and saw CPU usage hovering around 35 percent. Checked cgroup throttle metrics via direct inspection and confirmed significant cpu.stat throttling values.
root_cause: The container CPU quota was restricted too tightly relative to the thread pool size, causing lock contention and scheduler delays.
resolution: Increased the CPU limit from 2 cores to 8 cores to match the node capacity and eliminate scheduler throttling.

title: Model training evaluation pods stuck in container configuration failure
reported_symptoms: Our evaluation suite jobs fail to start when scheduled. Pods remain stuck in CreateContainerConfigError status indefinitely.
investigation: Inspected pod YAML specifications and runtime errors. Output indicated: Error syncing pod, skipping: failed to prepare subPath for volumeMount because secret "s3-evaluation-creds" was not found.
root_cause: A typo introduced in the storage access secret name during a recent security hardening ticket.
resolution: Corrected the secret name reference in the deployment manifest and recreated the required secret resource in the cluster.

title: Stable Diffusion Backend Crash Loop
reported_symptoms: Every time we send a burst of image generation requests, the pods suddenly terminate and restart. Our users are getting random 502 bad gateway errors.
investigation: Reviewed pod descriptions and found frequent restarts with Exit Code 137. Log snippet: [Init] Warming up diffusion pipeline... followed by kubelet killing the container due to failed HTTP health checks during heavy GPU tensor initialization.
root_cause: Concurrent CUDA context creation spikes CPU and GPU utilization, causing the health check endpoint to time out because the main thread is blocked.
resolution: Adjusted the livenessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 120 and added a startupProbe to isolate the heavy initialization period from active health monitoring.

title: Dashboard API backend restarting randomly under load
reported_symptoms: Users are experiencing random 502 Bad Gateway errors. The backend pods seem to reboot every few minutes.
investigation: Executed kubectl top pods and noticed memory usage pegged at 4Gi, matching the limit. Reviewed Kubernetes events showing repeated OOMKilled events on all backend replicas.
root_cause: A newly deployed caching layer was configured to store unlimited objects in memory.
resolution: Added a maximum cache size restriction in the application code and bumped memory limits to 8Gi.

title: Real-time fraud detection service crashing during traffic spikes
reported_symptoms: Our fraud scoring service goes down whenever transaction volume doubles. We suspect network timeouts.
investigation: Ran kubectl describe pod fraud-detect-v2-84b79. Observed Last State: Terminated with Exit Code 137. Prometheus metrics showed working set memory hitting the 8Gi limit consistently prior to crashes.
root_cause: In-memory lookup cache grew unbounded during high throughput events, triggering the kernel OOM killer.
resolution: Implemented TTL-based eviction on the lookup cache and raised container memory limits to 16Gi.

title: Model monitoring metrics scraper failure
reported_symptoms: Grafana dashboards show complete data loss for all GPU telemetry metrics. The Prometheus target status page lists all scrape targets as down with TLS errors.
investigation: Queried Prometheus targets API and found 'Get https://gpu-metrics-exporter.ml-ns.svc:9443/metrics: x509: certificate has expired'. Checked the exporter deployment and verified its serving certificate was past its expiry timestamp.
root_cause: The Prometheus exporter uses a sidecar that generates a self-signed cert valid for only 30 days, and the auto-rotation script crashed silently.
resolution: Updated the sidecar container image to the latest version with robust certificate auto-renewal logic and restarted the pods.

title: Web backend deployment stuck at initialization phase
reported_symptoms: We pushed an emergency hotfix to our backend API, but the new pods are hanging indefinitely in ContainerCreating state. Network policies must be blocking the storage backend.
investigation: Ran kubectl describe pod backend-api-deployment-7f99b. Output revealed: Warning FailedAttachVolume ... AttachVolume.Attach failed for 12345-abcde: Volume already attached to node gpu-worker-02.
root_cause: The rolling update strategy spawned the new pod before the old pod's container termination sequence fully unmounted the RWO volume.
resolution: Deleted the terminating old pod to release the volume lock immediately, allowing the new deployment pod to mount successfully.

title: Image processing pipeline timing out on thumbnail generation
reported_symptoms: Uploaded images are not generating thumbnails. Worker pods log upstream timeout errors when communicating with the storage cluster.
investigation: Reviewed pod logs: ERROR: ClientNetworkError: Connector timeout connecting to object storage endpoint. Checked cluster DNS resolution and endpoint connectivity; internal DNS lookup succeeded, but object storage throttled connections.
root_cause: The shared object storage service applied aggressive rate limiting due to an unexpected surge in parallel write operations from another tenant sharing the cluster zone.
resolution: Migrated the media processor to a dedicated object storage bucket endpoint with higher IOPS limits and added exponential backoff retry logic to the worker code.

title: API Gateway throwing 504 Gateway Timeouts on inference routes
reported_symptoms: Our clients are receiving 504 errors on almost all POST requests to the llm-inference endpoint. We checked our app and nothing changed on our side.
investigation: Checked ingress controller access logs and found numerous upstream request timeouts. Ran kubectl describe pods -n production-llm and verified pods are running with zero restarts. Inspected istio-proxy sidecar logs: upstream_cluster: llm-backend, response_code: 504, response_flags: UT.
root_cause: The downstream model serving cluster experienced high latency spikes after rolling out an unoptimized tensor parallel weight config, causing the gateway proxy to breach its timeout threshold.
resolution: Rolled back the model container deployment to the previous stable image tag and increased the ingress upstream read timeout from 30s to 60s temporarily.

title: Model monitoring dashboard intermittent service lookup failures
reported_symptoms: Prometheus targets are flapping between UP and DOWN states with context deadline exceeded and lookup errors against exporter pods.
investigation: Checked Prometheus targets page showing widespread scrape failures. Reviewed CoreDNS error logs and observed UDP packet drops due to conntrack table saturation on the host nodes.
root_cause: High volume of Prometheus scrape discovery queries exhausted the Linux kernel connection tracking table for DNS traffic, causing dropped UDP queries.
resolution: Deployed NodeLocal DNSCache to handle local TCP/UDP queries via loopback, bypassing iptables conntrack limits, and increased the net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max sysctl value.

title: Kubernetes control plane node migration failing
reported_symptoms: Ops automation reported a timeout while draining worker nodes for operating system patching. Redis pods refuse to leave the target host.
investigation: Queried eviction API responses via kubectl get events --field-selector reason=EvictionBlocked. Found that redis-ha-pdb had minAvailable set equal to the replica count, blocking all evictions.
root_cause: The high-availability Redis chart installed a strict PDB that prohibited single-pod evictions during node maintenance.
resolution: Edited the PDB configuration to reduce minAvailable by one, enabling successful pod eviction and letting the node drain proceed.

title: Intermittent DNS timeouts during batch data pipeline execution
reported_symptoms: Our nightly Spark jobs are failing randomly with java.net.UnknownHostException when talking to internal Postgres and S3 endpoints. It seems to happen more when the cluster scales up.
investigation: Checked application logs confirming intermittent name resolution failures. Inspected cluster DNS metrics and found CoreDNS request latency spiking. Ran kubectl logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns to check for errors and observed frequent SERVFAIL responses during peak hours.
root_cause: CoreDNS replicas were underprovisioned for the high volume of parallel lookups generated by our large Spark deployment, causing request queue saturation.
resolution: Scaled up CoreDNS deployment from 2 to 6 replicas and deployed NodeLocal DNSCache daemonset to alleviate load on the central cluster DNS server.

title: PyTorch Distributed Training Rollout Timeout
reported_symptoms: Training job deployments are failing because rollout never finishes. The nodes have plenty of VRAM, but pods hang indefinitely in not ready state.
investigation: Ran describe on stuck pods. Observed TCP socket connection timeouts on the custom status port. Snippet: Readiness probe failed: Get http://10.244.4.12:9090/ready: net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection.
root_cause: The training initialization script blocks the main event loop during dataset loading, preventing the HTTP health check server from starting before the initial delay elapsed.
resolution: Increased initialDelaySeconds from 10 to 60 to allow the dataset preparation phase to complete before probe execution begins.

title: Intermittent Image Pull Failures on Llama Inference Cluster
reported_symptoms: Our inference pods are stuck in ErrImagePull. Every few scale-ups, downloading weights fails randomly across different worker nodes.
investigation: Checked pod descriptions which revealed Back-off pulling image errors. Inspected containerd logs: 'failed to resolve image: pull request failed: 429 Too Many Requests'. Verified that our deployments lack registry credentials.
root_cause: Unauthenticated requests to Docker Hub from multiple auto-scaling nodes exceeded the anonymous tier rate limits.
resolution: Created a pull-through registry mirror and attached a secret containing authorized credentials to the default service account.

title: Customer portal backend throwing container config errors
reported_symptoms: Half of our web backend pods are failing health checks and restarting endlessly. Users report intermittent gateway timeouts.
investigation: Queried cluster state using kubectl get pods. Observed pods cycling through CreateContainerConfigError. Described a failing pod: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "jwt-keys": secret "auth-jwt-secret" not found.
root_cause: Security team's automated secret rotation script dropped the required token key during the latest rotation cycle.
resolution: Manually re-added the missing token key to the existing secret object in the cluster, resolving the initialization failures.

title: Real-time fraud detection service unable to deploy new version
reported_symptoms: We pushed a hotfix for our fraud scoring engine, but the new pods won't deploy. Old pods are still running thankfully.
investigation: Checked deployment rollout status. Encountered error message: secrets "stripe-webhook-keys" not found. Checked etcd via kubectl and verified the secret object was entirely missing.
root_cause: The secret was removed during an audit of unused keys last week, failing to account for this active service dependency.
resolution: Re-imported the secret from our master password manager and triggered a manual rollout restart.

title: Training job webhook rejection on PyTorchOperator
reported_symptoms: We are unable to submit any new multi-node PyTorch jobs. The API server returns internal errors when processing our custom resource definitions.
investigation: Reviewed webhook configuration and pod logs for the training operator. Observed connection refusals and TLS validation failures. Executed 'openssl s_client -connect training-webhook-svc.kubeflow.svc:443' which explicitly reported an expired certificate chain.
root_cause: The mutating webhook CA bundle was signed by an internal CA that expired after 90 days without automated rotation.
resolution: Generated a new CA bundle, patched the MutatingWebhookConfiguration object, and restarted the training operator deployment.

title: Web backend API gateway failing internal service discovery
reported_symptoms: Our ingress controller is returning 504 Gateway Timeouts for backend microservices. The error logs indicate it cannot resolve downstream service names in the cluster.
investigation: Checked core DNS pod status and saw frequent restarts with exit code 137. Ran kubectl describe pod -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns confirming OOMKilled events following memory spikes.
root_cause: Memory leaks in older CoreDNS version combined with high query concurrency from the gateway led to repeated pod crashes and intermittent outages.
resolution: Upgraded CoreDNS image to the latest stable release, provisioned dedicated memory headroom, and implemented NodeLocal DNSCache.

title: LLM Inference API replicas stuck at zero during traffic spike
reported_symptoms: Our customer-facing chat endpoints stopped scaling up right when latency started to climb. New pods are not being scheduled at all, though our existing instances are processing requests until they crash from overload.
investigation: I checked the deployment status and noticed desired replicas are set to ten, but available count remains at two. Running kubectl describe deployment showed persistent warnings: 0/12 nodes available: pods quota exceeded. Checked namespace limits via kubectl describe quota and confirmed CPU and memory allocations have hit maximum limits.
root_cause: The production namespace had exhausted its allocated memory resource quota, preventing the Kubernetes scheduler from provisioning new replica pods.
resolution: Increased the namespace memory quota limit from 64Gi to 128Gi after getting approval from the platform lead, which allowed the waiting pods to schedule immediately.

title: Batch ETL Worker Nodes Failing to Spawn
reported_symptoms: Nightly data processing jobs are failing because worker containers refuse to download. We suspect a network glitch.
investigation: Inspected node diagnostic bundles. Node logs explicitly showed docker daemon rejecting pulls with 'toomanyrequests: Too Many Requests'. Network connectivity was completely fine.
root_cause: Concurrent scaling of hundreds of batch workers triggered rate limiting on the public image repository provider.
resolution: Injected imagePullSecrets into the Argo workflows and staggered pod startup times to flatten the request spike.

title: Mixtral fine-tuning hangs on barrier sync
reported_symptoms: Our multi-node Mixtral fine-tune died abruptly. The error message mentions a watchdog timeout in ncclCommInitRank. We think it might be an out-of-memory issue on the master node.
investigation: Queried Kubernetes events and pod logs.kubectl logs mixtral-worker-3 showed NCCL WARN: Call to connect returned Connection refused. Ran ibstat on the suspect host and verified that port state was listed as Down instead of Active.
root_cause: Subnet manager dropped the physical link on node-k9-n03 due to excessive bit error rates, isolating it from the master node during initialization.
resolution: Marked node-k9-n03 as unschedulable, alerted datacenter operations to inspect the fiber patch cable, and advised the client to relaunch their job.

title: Distributed training job failing to initialize nodes
reported_symptoms: Hey support, our multi-node LLM pre-training run aborted immediately after submission. The master node logs mention something about pulling images, but our Dockerfile builds fine locally.
investigation: Ran kubectl describe pod pytorch-master-0 and noted the Event stream showing Back-off pulling image "nvcr.io/private/train:latest-patch2". Verified image existence in the registry api; the tag was absent.
root_cause: The automated build job in GitHub Actions failed silently, so the new image was never pushed before the Kubernetes job was triggered.
resolution: Triggered a manual rebuild in CI, confirmed successful registry push, and restarted the training job successfully.

title: Vector Database Pods Failing Health Checks
reported_symptoms: Our vector database nodes are caught in an endless restart loop in the production namespace. Queries are failing intermittently.
investigation: Ran kubectl get pods -w and noticed status flipping to CrashLoopBackOff. Examined kubectl describe events: Liveness probe failed: Get http://10.244.1.95:9091/healthz: dial tcp: connection refused. Application logs showed normal index loading activity.
root_cause: The default liveness probe interval was too tight for the large index segment replay sequence executed upon startup.
resolution: Configured a startupProbe with a 240-second timeout window and tuned the liveness probe period to 20 seconds.

title: Batch ETL processing pods failing with database timeout exceptions
reported_symptoms: Our scheduled data warehouse loader pod failed again tonight. The logs just show database connection timeout errors after 300 seconds.
investigation: Checked cronjob history and logs. Found the following trace: sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit overflow. Inspected database metrics dashboard and observed connection pool exhaustion coinciding with the etl start time.
root_cause: An inefficient migration script deployed earlier in the evening locked critical metadata tables, preventing the ETL workers from acquiring database connections within the allocated window.
resolution: Reverted the problematic database migration, killed lingering orphaned queries, and restarted the ETL cron pod successfully.

title: Web frontend user dashboard returns 504 Gateway Timeouts
reported_symptoms: Users report that loading their profile dashboard results in a blank page and browser console shows 504 Gateway Timeouts from the backend API.
investigation: Inspected backend pod metrics and saw normal CPU/RAM utilization. Checked upstream dependency health checks and found the user-auth-service was failing health probes intermittently due to slow LDAP lookups.
root_cause: The external LDAP identity provider experienced severe network latency, causing the user authentication service to hang while verifying session tokens.
resolution: Switched the authentication service to fall back to cached JWT validation during LDAP degradation and notified the network team.

title: Computer vision model training pods stuck
reported_symptoms: Our image classification training run refuses to start. The job scheduler logs show no active errors, just waiting.
investigation: Inspected kube-scheduler logs and ran kubectl describe pods. Discovered recurrent errors: '0/15 nodes are available: 15 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu'. Node status showed zero free GPUs across all available zones.
root_cause: Simultaneous execution of multiple heavy research jobs saturated every available GPU node in the cluster region.
resolution: Provisioned an on-demand cluster autoscaler group with L4 GPUs and migrated the training job to the newly created capacity.

title: API gateway crashing repeatedly after secret rotation
reported_symptoms: All API backend pods entered CrashLoopBackOff status immediately after we rotated our database credentials secret.
investigation: Queried logs of the failing pod: kubectl logs api-gateway-55df9-x2trw --previous. Output showed: sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.OperationalError) fe_sendauth: no password supplied.
root_cause: The secret key name in Kubernetes was inadvertently changed from DATABASE_PASSWORD to DB_PASS, causing the application to look for an empty environment variable.
resolution: Updated the secret reference keys in the deployment yaml to match the application's expected environment variable names.

title: GPU driver update stalled on deep learning cluster
reported_symptoms: Automatic node pool update for NVIDIA driver upgrades is stuck. Nodes remain in cordoned state with zero progress.
investigation: Checked node drain output displaying waiting for pods: tf-serving-deployment-559db-abc12. Checked PDB rules: minAvailable was configured to 4 out of 4 pods, preventing any single pod from being evicted.
root_cause: The deployment relied on a strict PDB that left no margin for rolling maintenance operations.
resolution: Temporarily scaled up the deployment replicas to five, allowing the eviction safety check to pass, and completed the node driver update.

title: Inference API pods stuck in ImagePullBackOff after morning rollout
reported_symptoms: Our production text generation API is completely down. We pushed a hotfix an hour ago and now zero replicas are running. They are just throwing errors on startup.
investigation: Checked pod statuses across the cluster using kubectl get pods. Observed multiple instances in ImagePullBackOff. Inspected the failing deployment yaml and found an invalid tag v2.4.1-rc3 which was never pushed to the private container registry.
root_cause: Typo in the image tag reference within the deployment manifest pointing to a non-existent artifact version.
resolution: Rolled back the deployment to the stable v2.4.0 release via helm rollback, and notified the developer to correct the image tag in their CI pipeline.

title: PyTorch training job stuck downloading weights
reported_symptoms: Worker nodes for our distributed run are throwing connection timeouts when hitting our private model registry. Names look up fine via nslookup, but data won't flow.
investigation: Executed diagnostic commands inside the active worker pod. $ curl -v http://model-registry.storage.svc.cluster.local:8080/health. Connection timed out. Reviewed recent cluster hardening applied by security team. Discovered default isolation policies dropped cross-namespace traffic.
root_cause: A newly enforced NetworkPolicy severed inter-namespace communication without a corresponding allow rule for the training jobs.
resolution: Updated the target namespace ingress rules to explicitly permit traffic originating from the trainer pods to the storage registry.

title: Batch ETL pipeline authentication crash
reported_symptoms: Our nightly Spark jobs are dropping database connections and failing to securely push processed vectors to the object store.
investigation: Queried driver pod logs and identified repeated SSL routines: 'certificate verify failed: certificate has expired'. Verified the truststore mounted in the executor pods contained an outdated enterprise root certificate.
root_cause: The automated certificate distribution cronjob failed to push the newly renewed enterprise root CA to the spark worker namespaces.
resolution: Manually updated the truststore ConfigMap across affected namespaces and restarted the active SparkApplication instances.

title: Distributed PyTorch Training Stalled on Worker 3
reported_symptoms: Distributed training job stopped advancing during epoch 12. Rank 3 is not responding to NCCL heartbeats.
investigation: Examined training logs for rank 3 and observed fatal segmentation faults tied to libcuda.so. Executed kubectl logs on the daemonset nvidia-device-plugin and saw continuous health check failures for GPU index 1. Checked kernel buffer ring and identified Xid 43 errors indicating a dropped GPU interrupt.
root_cause: Unrecoverable hardware interrupt failure on accelerator slot 1 triggering driver crash.
resolution: Drained the compute instance completely. Performed a hard reboot of the host machine to clear the PCIe lane lockup.

title: Distributed Diffusion training timeout error
reported_symptoms: We keep getting random NCCL watchdog timeouts during our text-to-image training runs. The job runs fine for about twenty minutes and then suddenly crashes with unhelpful stack traces pointing to PyTorch DDP.
investigation: Inspected pod metrics via Prometheus and observed high latency spikes on specific network interfaces. Executed nvidia-smi topo -m to verify NVLink status, which looked nominal. Checked kernel logs on worker nodes: dmesg | grep -i ib showed InfiniBand link flaps specifically on node-b2-n05.
root_cause: Flapping InfiniBand link on node-b2-n05 caused intermittent packet loss, breaking ring reduction sequences and triggering NCCL timeouts.
resolution: Isolated node-b2-n05 from the active allocation pool, ran diagnostic nccl-tests successfully on remaining nodes, and restarted the training pipeline.

title: Stable Diffusion WebUI Unreachable After Update
reported_symptoms: After pushing our latest image generation backend update, the ingress controller dropped all backends. The pods look healthy in the console.
investigation: Queried kubectl events and spotted persistent probe timeouts. Snippet: Readiness probe error: Get "http://10.244.2.88:7860/": context deadline exceeded.
root_cause: The updated application required explicit authentication headers for root path requests, causing the unauthenticated readiness probe to fail indefinitely.
resolution: Added a dedicated unauthenticated /health endpoint to the FastAPI app code and updated the deployment probe path to use it.

title: Batch ETL pipeline containers failing to boot up
reported_symptoms: Our nightly batch processing job failed completely. The driver pod won't start up and our SLAs are ticking. Please check if the cluster has network issues reaching the registry.
investigation: Ran kubectl get pods -n spark-jobs and saw ImagePullBackOff. Checked node network connectivity to the container registry; traffic was normal. Inspected pod description which revealed an attempt to pull a deleted image sha.
root_cause: Recent registry cleanup policy pruned the specific image digest referenced by the static Kubernetes cronjob manifest.
resolution: Updated the cronjob template to point to the active daily tag instead of the pruned digest and forced a job run.

title: Real-time LLM chat frontend API unreachable
reported_symptoms: Users report that the chat UI cannot reach the backend API server. The ingress is throwing 503 Service Temporarily Unavailable errors.
investigation: Inspected ingress backend status and saw 0/1 endpoints available. Executed kubectl describe endpoints frontend-api-service and verified it was empty. Cross-referenced the pod labels against the service spec and discovered a typo where the service selector had env=production but pods were tagged environment=production.
root_cause: Mismatched label keys in the service selector configuration.
resolution: Fixed the service selector key from env to environment, successfully binding the pods as endpoints.

title: Distributed training workload crashes on startup after code push
reported_symptoms: Worker nodes for our distributed training job keep crashing instantly. The coordinator node is waiting for workers that never show up.
investigation: Examined pod lifecycle events via kubectl get events. Logged error: Error: secret "wandb-api-key" not found. Confirmed the training job manifest references a secret key that no longer exists.
root_cause: Recent refactoring of the Helm chart renamed the Weights and Biases secret key reference without provisioning the corresponding new key.
resolution: Created the expected secret key in the target namespace and restarted the training job pods.

title: Audio Transcription Pods Throwing CUDA Errors
reported_symptoms: All pods on node audio-node-02 are failing to load models into GPU memory, throwing invalid device ordinal exceptions.
investigation: Ran kubectl get pods -o wide and isolated failures to audio-node-02. Inspected kernel messages and spotted critical Xid 74 thermal or physical drop errors. Confirmed device driver lost communication with the physical board.
root_cause: Hardware component failure resulting in the device dropping off the internal PCIe switch.
resolution: Isolated the node from the cluster, drained active jobs, and filed an RMA ticket for the defective accelerator card.

title: LLaMA-70B pretraining stalled on collective ops
reported_symptoms: Our 64-node distributed pretraining job froze entirely overnight. Every pod is stuck at step 14200 and there has been zero throughput for hours. Could you check if the storage backend is choking our checkpoint writes?
investigation: Checked GPU operator logs and found persistent fatal errors. Ran kubectl describe pods -n ml-jobs and discovered watchdog triggers. Reviewed NCCL debug logs: WARN: [send] Connection reset by peer on ib0. Checked switch telemetry and confirmed intermittent packet drops on leaf 4.
root_cause: A deteriorating QSFP transceiver on node-r4-n12 induced massive InfiniBand packet drops, stalling all-reduce synchronization across the ring.
resolution: Cordoned node-r4-n12, notified hardware maintenance for transceiver replacement, and instructed the customer to resume training from the latest S3 checkpoint.

title: Web frontend failing to communicate with session broker
reported_symptoms: Users report login errors. Frontend logs show connection timeouts when talking to the session-broker service. DNS resolution is fine, but TCP connections never establish.
investigation: Ran diagnostic port probes from a running frontend pod. $ timeout 5 bash -c '</dev/tcp/session-broker.auth.svc.cluster.local/6379'. No route to host / timed out. Checked applied security manifests and discovered a missing allow directive in the namespace policy.
root_cause: A default-deny NetworkPolicy applied to the authentication namespace prevented the frontend pods from establishing socket connections.
resolution: Drafted a specific NetworkPolicy permitting inbound TCP connections on port 6379 from the frontend namespace to the session broker.

title: Vector database nodes unable to boot after cluster scaling event
reported_symptoms: Embeddings searches are timing out. The autoscaler tried spinning up new index pods but they are stuck in pending or configuration error loops.
investigation: Ran kubectl describe pod on the failing instances. Output showed: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "db-credentials": secret "vector-db-auth" not found. Verified namespace contents; the secret was missing.
root_cause: An accidental manual deletion of the database authentication secret during routine namespace cleanup.
resolution: Restored the deleted secret from our backup secret store operator and verified pods transitioned to running state within seconds.

title: Milvus vector search pods failing deployment update
reported_symptoms: Tried rolling out a configuration update for our indexing nodes, but the rollout is hung. Old pods are still running, but no new pods are appearing in the cluster view.
investigation: Reviewed the rollout status using kubectl rollout history. Checked replica set events for the deployment and found repeated errors reading: Error creating: pods quota exceeded. Inspected namespace quota objects and verified GPU count allocation was pegged at the maximum threshold.
root_cause: Rolling updates temporarily require double the resource capacity to perform zero-downtime replacements, which breached the strict GPU resource quota ceiling.
resolution: Adjusted the deployment strategy maxSurge parameter to zero to prevent parallel pod creation, and requested a temporary quota increase from the infrastructure team.

title: Vector database cluster migration halted on persistent volume claim
reported_symptoms: Our Milvus vector database replicas are failing readiness probes after node maintenance. Pods are throwing mount volume errors. Is our disk corrupted?
investigation: Inspected persistent volume claims: kubectl describe pvc vector-data-pvc. Found status as Bound, but pod events showed: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "pvc-vector-data-pvc" : rpc error: code = Internal desc = Volume is already mounted by another node.
root_cause: Graceful node drain timed out before the previous Kubernetes node finished unmounting the block device.
resolution: Manually detached the block storage volume from the decommissioned compute node via API and recycled the stuck replica pod.

title: Kafka consumer pods dropping heartbeats due to DNS lag
reported_symptoms: Kafka consumers are rebalancing constantly and throwing socket timeout exceptions when trying to resolve broker endpoints in our custom namespace.
investigation: Inspected /etc/resolv.conf inside the consumer pods and verified search path length. Ran dig @10.96.0.10 kafka-broker-0.kafka.svc.cluster.local and noticed intermittent 5-second delays.
root_cause: Excessive ndots setting in pod configurations forced recursive lookups through multiple search domains before hitting the correct service name, timing out under load.
resolution: Updated the Helm chart for the streaming pipeline to explicitly set ndots:1 in the pod spec and deployed NodeLocal DNSCache to cache responses locally.

title: GPU node replacement stuck on distributed training job
reported_symptoms: We have a multi-node training run that cannot finish because the underlying host is failing hardware checks, but the scheduler refuses to evacuate the pod.
investigation: Ran kubectl get events and spotted repeated errors: Eviction failed: Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod disruption budget. Inspected the PDB manifest and found maxUnavailable set to 0 explicitly to protect checkpointing stability.
root_cause: An overly restrictive PodDisruptionBudget configuration completely prevented Kubernetes from evicting the training worker pod from the degraded node.
resolution: Temporarily patched the PDB to allow one unavailable pod, let the node drain successfully, and then restored the original PDB setting.

title: Distributed training workers losing heartbeat during gradient sync
reported_symptoms: Our multi-node training job keeps failing because worker 3 loses connection to the master node during AllReduce steps. The error log just says context deadline exceeded.
investigation: Looked at dmesg and system logs on the worker node with no hardware errors found. Inspected Kubernetes events and noticed frequent SIGKILL events. Checked container telemetry and found massive CFS throttle counts accumulating rapidly during matrix multiplication phases.
root_cause: CPU limits were set too aggressively on the training pods, causing the background NCCL communication threads to be starved of CPU time slices.
resolution: Adjusted the Kubernetes pod resource specification to remove the CPU limit entirely while keeping the request intact.

title: Customer portal backend deployment failing after autoscaling event
reported_symptoms: Users are reporting 502 bad gateway errors on our main application portal. It looks like the horizontal pod autoscaler tried to scale out, but no new backend pods were created.
investigation: Queried events in the web-production namespace with kubectl get events --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp'. Found continuous FailedCreate events due to exceeded resource quota limits on object counts.
root_cause: The total number of active pods and configmaps in the namespace crossed the maximum object count threshold enforced by the platform governance policy.
resolution: Pruned old unused ConfigMaps and Secret revisions left behind by previous CI/CD deployments, freeing up quota space for new application pods.

title: Real-time Fraud Detection Pipeline Stalled
reported_symptoms: Kafka consumer pods are running on GPU worker nodes, but lag is skyrocketing because the deployment rollout has stalled completely.
investigation: Checked pod status and discovered failing TCP socket checks. Snippet: Readiness probe failed: dial tcp 10.244.6.14:5000: connect: no route to host.
root_cause: A recent network policy update blocked internal traffic on port 5000, which the readiness probe was attempting to reach for health verification.
resolution: Updated the cluster network policies to allow internal health check traffic to reach the application port on worker nodes.

title: GPT-NeoX training run freezing mid-epoch
reported_symptoms: Our 32-node training job locks up completely during gradient synchronization. No OOM logs anywhere. It just hangs indefinitely until our orchestration timeout kills it.
investigation: Traced network traffic across the cluster fabric. Log excerpt: NCCL WARN Network is unreachable while attempting to resolve peer addresses. Inspected ethtool statistics and discovered extreme CRC errors accumulating on node-c1-n08.
root_cause: Degraded network interface card firmware on node-c1-n08 caused silent packet corruption, leading to permanent stalls in collective communication primitives.
resolution: Evicted all workloads from node-c1-n08, scheduled firmware update, and confirmed the client successfully restarted training from checkpoint.

title: Backend API rollout hanging indefinitely
reported_symptoms: We pushed a rolling update to our user management API, but new pods never start and traffic is dropping.
investigation: Queried deployment status and ran kubectl describe. Output indicated: '0/8 nodes are available: 8 Insufficient cpu'. CPU requests per pod were set to 4 cores, but nodes only had 2 unallocated cores remaining.
root_cause: Overly aggressive CPU resource requests combined with maxed-out node resource allocations prevented the scheduler from placing the rolling update pods.
resolution: Reduced CPU requests from 4 to 1.5 cores, matching historical load testing baselines, and completed the rollout.

title: Inference API returning 503 Service Unavailable
reported_symptoms: Our client application keeps getting connection refused errors when hitting the vLLM endpoint inside the cluster, despite all replicas showing green status.
investigation: Checked pod states and saw all four replicas Running and Ready. Inspected the Kubernetes endpoints object for the service using kubectl get endpoints vllm-api-svc and found zero addresses listed. Compared the service selector labels against the pod labels and noticed the service was targeting app=vllm-prod while the pods were tagged app=vllm-production.
root_cause: Typo in the Service object selector label causing endpoint generation failure.
resolution: Updated the selector in the Service YAML to match the pod labels exactly.

title: Model Fine-Tuning Jobs Throwing Pull Errors
reported_symptoms: Our fine-tuning jobs fail right at the start. The pods cannot fetch the base PyTorch image from Docker Hub.
investigation: Ran journalctl -u kubelet on the worker node and located HTTP 429 responses during the image layer download phase.
root_cause: Shared cluster IP address reached the maximum threshold of anonymous pull requests allowed by the registry operator.
resolution: Configured cluster-level image pull secrets and forced all namespaces to pull through our internal authenticated mirror.

title: Web backend pods throwing image pull errors during autoscaling
reported_symptoms: Traffic spike hit our service and the horizontal pod autoscaler tried to scale up, but the new pods are stuck and throwing weird container creation errors.
investigation: Executed kubectl get events --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp' and located repeated warnings: Failed to pull image "registry.internal/apps/gateway:1.14.9": tag does not exist. The existing running pods were fine, but new replicas failed.
root_cause: A recent merge to main updated the deployment manifest with a future version number before the Jenkins publish stage completed.
resolution: Performed a kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway to revert to version 1.14.8 until the CI/CD pipeline finished building the new release.

title: Intermittent timeouts on text-embedding inference pods
reported_symptoms: Our embedding service is dropping connections every few minutes under moderate load. Health probes are failing and Kubernetes keeps restarting pods randomly. We think there might be a memory leak or a database bottleneck.
investigation: Checked pod logs and found zero errors prior to termination. Reviewed node metrics and saw steady CPU utilization around 40 percent. Inspected cgroup stats inside the container and discovered severe CFS throttling: cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.stat showed nr_throttled in the tens of thousands.
root_cause: The container spec had a restrictive CPU limit of 1 core while requests were set to 4, triggering aggressive Completely Fair Scheduler throttling during tokenization bursts.
resolution: Removed the strict CPU limit from the deployment manifest and let the workload burst freely using node headroom.

title: Vector search cluster deployment failing init phase
reported_symptoms: We are trying to deploy the new vector search tier for our search engine, but all pods are failing to schedule. The status column says ErrImagePull.
investigation: Examined pod events using kubectl describe. Output showed: Failed to pull image "corp-docker.internal/vector/milvus:v2.5.0-beta": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Error response from daemon: manifest for corp-docker.internal/vector/milvus:v2.5.0-beta not found. Checked artifact repository and confirmed only v2.5.0 exists.
root_cause: Customer included an unreleased beta suffix in the Kubernetes manifest that did not match the actual built image tag.
resolution: Updated the deployment configuration to use the correct v2.5.0 tag and applied the changes.

title: Distributed PyTorch training jobs losing connection to coordinator
reported_symptoms: Worker nodes in our distributed training run are dropping out because they can't resolve the hostname of the torchrun master node. Training aborts after a few minutes.
investigation: Traced packet drops via tcpdump inside the container network namespace. Looked at CoreDNS logs and found throttling due to CPU limits being hit. Checked metrics showing CPU throttling above 80 percent on DNS pods.
root_cause: CoreDNS CPU throttling during massive startup synchronization storms where hundreds of workers simultaneously queried the master hostname.
resolution: Removed CPU limits on CoreDNS deployment, added Horizontal Pod Autoscaler for CoreDNS based on CPU utilization, and tuned client retry intervals.

title: Distributed Training Job Crashed Mid-Epoch
reported_symptoms: Checkpoint saving failed and rank 4 of our multi-node job stopped responding. The entire training run looks dead.
investigation: Inspected node telemetry and discovered worker-gpu-14 dropped off the network. SSH access failed. Serial console logs indicated a hard kernel lockup during PCIe link training.
root_cause: Hardware PCIe bus error triggered a kernel panic, freezing the OS and stopping the local kubelet service.
resolution: Isolated the faulty machine, removed it from the active Kubernetes scheduler pool, and requested hardware replacement from data center operations.

title: Web frontend gateway SSL drop
reported_symptoms: Users visiting our dashboard are greeted with browser security warnings about invalid security certificates.
investigation: Examined NGINX ingress controller error logs revealing 'SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:1416F086:SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed)'. Checked ingress resource and noticed the secret reference pointed to an unmanaged expired asset.
root_cause: The automated certificate sync daemon failed to bind the newly issued certificate from Vault to the Kubernetes ingress resource.
resolution: Restarted the HashiCorp Vault Agent Injector pod and forced a refresh of the ingress TLS secret mapping.

title: PyTorch Distributed Training Job Restarts
reported_symptoms: Worker pods in our multi-node distributed training job are dying unexpectedly. We suspect a network partition between the GPU worker nodes.
investigation: Checked container logs and found no traceback, only sudden termination. Kubernetes events displayed: Back-off restarting failed container worker-0. Node pressure metrics showed normal CPU and memory thresholds.
root_cause: The NCCL initialization phase takes longer than the liveness probe threshold allows, leading the kubelet to prematurely terminate healthy worker processes.
resolution: Added a startup probe with a high failure threshold to allow full distributed cluster rendezvous before liveness checks begin.

title: Inference API TLS handshake failures
reported_symptoms: Our client applications cannot reach the LLM endpoint anymore. All requests fail immediately with TLS handshake errors and something about x509 expiration.
investigation: Checked ingress controller logs and found recurring error entries: 'x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid'. Inspected the secret vllm-tls-cert using kubectl describe and confirmed the Not After date was yesterday.
root_cause: The cert-manager automated renewal process stalled due to a transient Route53 DNS validation timeout.
resolution: Triggered a manual certificate renewal via cert-manager and updated the Let's Encrypt cluster issuer configuration.

title: Computer vision model inference pipeline lagging behind queue
reported_symptoms: The video frame processing queue is backing up rapidly. Workers are processing frames much slower than the camera streams produce them. GPU utilization is surprisingly low at around 15 percent.
investigation: Traced the data pipeline and discovered that image decoding and preprocessing threads were bottlenecked. Checked container metrics and found that cpu throttling was consuming over 40 percent of allocated CPU time.
root_cause: CPU limits were clamped too low for the preprocessing containers, preventing them from feeding frames to the GPU fast enough.
resolution: Removed the CPU limit from the preprocessing container definition, allowing full utilization of available core capacity.

title: API pods terminating unexpectedly during peak load
reported_symptoms: Our customer-facing inference pods are constantly crashing with no clear stack trace. We think it might be a memory leak in the latest model weights.
investigation: Checked pod termination statuses. Found multiple restarts with exit code 137. Ran kubectl describe pod tensor-serve-7b89f-2xqzp and observed OOMKilled: true, Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOM. Prometheus showed memory consumption spiking to the exact 16Gi limit right before termination.
root_cause: Increased concurrent request batch size exhausted the allocated container memory limit.
resolution: Increased container memory request and limit to 32Gi in the deployment manifest and applied the update.

title: Redis cache cluster replica replacement stuck
reported_symptoms: A node failure triggered an automatic failover for our caching layer, but the replacement replica pod is refusing to start up, leaving our cluster running in a degraded state.
investigation: Checked the operator logs and found persistent reconciliation errors. Ran kubectl describe pod redis-replica-2 and confirmed the failure message: FailedCreate: pods quota exceeded for CPU requests.
root_cause: Strict namespace quotas prevented the operator from spinning up a new replica pod to replace the crashed instance without violating the CPU request cap.
resolution: Elevated the CPU resource quota for the caching namespace and manually restarted the operator reconciliation loop to trigger immediate pod creation.

title: Graph analytics engine pods failing initial volume mount
reported_symptoms: Our Neo4j graph cluster nodes are failing readiness checks after a regional network blip. The storage volumes seem detached or missing entirely.
investigation: Executed kubectl get volumeattachments. Found an orphaned attachment record pointing to a dead worker node. Error: AttachFailed due to conflicting node assignment.
root_cause: Abnormal node termination left an active VolumeAttachment object dangling in the API server without a corresponding node object.
resolution: Manually patched and deleted the orphaned VolumeAttachment resource, permitting the scheduler to reattach the disk to the healthy node.

title: Cluster autoscaler unable to scale down idle nodes
reported_symptoms: Cluster autoscaler logs show it wants to remove empty nodes to save costs, but it keeps timing out trying to evict stateful pods.
investigation: Traced autoscaler diagnostics showing failed evictions on qdrant-node-0. Executed kubectl describe pdb qdrant-pdb which displayed minAvailable: 1 against a single replica statefulset, resulting in zero allowed disruptions.
root_cause: Stateful workload protection was configured with a PDB that disallowed any voluntary disruption, trapping the pod on a node targeted for scale-down.
resolution: Temporarily deleted the PDB object to let the node drain and downscale complete, then recreated the PDB with updated parameters.

title: Distributed training coordinator unreachable
reported_symptoms: Worker nodes cannot connect to the main training coordinator. Jobs are timing out during initialization and throwing connection refused exceptions.
investigation: Verified that the coordinator pod was healthy and listening on port 29500 via exec. Ran kubectl describe svc pytorch-coord-svc and observed that the Endpoints field was completely empty. Checked the pod metadata and realized the deployment template used training-role: coordinator, whereas the service selector expected role: coordinator.
root_cause: Key mismatch between the Service selector and the pod label keys.
resolution: Modified the service selector key from role to training-role to re-establish endpoint mapping.

title: Training Cluster Pods Failing with ErrImageNeverPull
reported_symptoms: Distributed training jobs are failing to start. The console says container runtime error, but the image exists in the public repo.
investigation: Ran kubectl describe pods and spotted repeated status codes 429 in the container runtime events. Checked cluster-wide pull traffic metrics and noted thousands of unauthenticated pulls hitting external registries.
root_cause: Massive parallel pod creation triggered public registry throttling due to missing authentication headers.
resolution: Configured imagePullSecrets across all namespaces and rotated personal access tokens for the container registry.

title: LLM generation latency spikes and liveness probe failures
reported_symptoms: Clients are reporting that text generation requests take ten times longer than usual. Sometimes the API gateway returns 504 Gateway Timeouts, yet application metrics show the model weights are loaded and GPU memory is half empty.
investigation: Queried Prometheus for container cpu throttling metrics and observed a massive spike matching the latency alerts. Executed kubectl exec to check container performance counters and confirmed high scheduling delays despite low overall node load.
root_cause: A recent configuration rollout imposed a tight CPU ceiling of 2000m on pods handling heavy tokenizer threads, causing thread starvation.
resolution: Rolled back the CPU ceiling reduction and updated the deployment template to allocate unconstrained CPU shares.

title: LLM Inference API throwing sudden no such host errors
reported_symptoms: Clients are getting 502 Bad Gateway intermittently. Our vLLM pods are complaining they cannot reach the internal Redis cache or model weight registry.
investigation: Executed kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns and noticed several CoreDNS pods had been OOMKilled recently due to memory limits. Examined dns traffic and saw massive lookup amplification caused by default search domains and high ndots settings.
root_cause: CoreDNS pods ran out of memory under heavy query load, triggering restarts, while high ndots settings caused excessive upstream queries for non-fully-qualified names.
resolution: Increased CoreDNS memory limits and CPU requests, updated the default pod dnsConfig to include options ndots:2, and enabled NodeLocal DNSCache across all worker nodes.

title: Batch ETL Processing Containers Terminating
reported_symptoms: Our nightly ETL pipelines crash right after starting up. The logs look clean until they abruptly stop.
investigation: Queried logs with kubectl logs --previous and saw successful data ingestion followed by kubelet killing the pod due to liveness check timeouts.
root_cause: Heavy disk I/O during initial cache hydration blocked the HTTP server thread answering the liveness probe.
resolution: Separated the health check handler onto a dedicated lightweight thread and introduced a startup probe with extended parameters.

title: Inference API connectivity failure to feature store
reported_symptoms: Our production inference pods cannot fetch vectors from the feature-db service anymore. They started timing out right after yesterday's security update. DNS is green.
investigation: Ran a quick check from the failing pod container. $ kubectl exec -it llm-serving-proxy-7b89-abc -- nc -zv feature-db.internal 5432. Timed out after thirty seconds. Checked cluster policies and found a newly applied default-deny ingress rule that lacked an exemption for the serving namespace.
root_cause: An overly restrictive Namespace-level NetworkPolicy blocked incoming TCP traffic on port 5432.
resolution: Created a specific NetworkPolicy resource allowing ingress from the llm-serving namespace to feature-db on port 5432.

title: Data preprocessing batch pods dying on boot
reported_symptoms: Our ETL pipeline containers fail to start up. The scheduler reports exit code 1 repeatedly.
investigation: Ran kubectl logs ray-head-node-765bf --tail=50 --previous. Found error trace: pydantic.error_wrappers.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Settings -> redis_port -> field required.
root_cause: The application update introduced strict schema validation expecting an explicit port definition that was omitted from the deployment manifest.
resolution: Added the missing redis_port environment variable to the Kubernetes deployment specification and verified clean startup.

title: Image rendering worker pods failing to schedule
reported_symptoms: Rendering tasks are stuck in ContainerCreating state or getting evicted immediately after scheduling. Logs show no application errors.
investigation: Ran kubectl describe node render-node-03. Found DiskPressure: true and message: Disk pressure detected on ephemeral storage. Inspected storage metrics showing disk utilization at 98 percent due to cached texture assets.
root_cause: Large texture assets downloaded by rendering jobs filled the local ephemeral storage without being properly cleaned up.
resolution: Cleared the asset cache directory, freed node disk space, and updated the pod specs to use shared object storage for large assets.

title: Inference API endpoint unresponsiveness due to storage volume lock
reported_symptoms: We deployed a new canary v2 model weight, but the pods won't start up. The HTTP 503 errors are cascading through our gateway. Maybe the NFS server is down?
investigation: Ran kubectl get pods -n inference. Noticed the volume state. Checked node logs: Journalctl showed CSI driver timeout error while attaching disk-8841. Multi-Attach error for volume pvc-vector-store detected on two distinct availability zones.
root_cause: Stale attach object left in the storage controller database preventing volume reattachment.
resolution: Cleaned up the dangling volume attachment CRD in Kubernetes and restarted the CSI node plugin daemonset pod on the target worker.

title: Batch ETL pipeline deployment failing on Kubernetes cluster
reported_symptoms: Nightly data warehouse sync didn't run. The cronjob spawned pods, but they all failed right away with container creation issues.
investigation: Pulled logs and status for the failed job execution. Found: Failed to inject env var from secret data-warehouse-creds: secret "data-warehouse-creds" not found. Checked secret list and confirmed total absence.
root_cause: A recent Terraform apply accidentally purged the ETL database credentials secret from the staging environment.
resolution: Applied the missing Terraform configuration to provision the secret resource, clearing the pod configuration errors.

title: Real-time fraud detection pipeline stalled
reported_symptoms: Flink task managers are failing to initialize in the production cluster, causing a backlog in transaction scoring.
investigation: Checked scheduler traces and pod descriptions. Encountered: 'FailedScheduling: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu'. Verified that all T4 GPU nodes were bound to legacy monitoring daemons.
root_cause: Taints applied to dedicated inference nodes rejected the incoming streaming pods, while general-purpose nodes lacked GPU hardware entirely.
resolution: Added the appropriate tolerations to the Flink job definitions and reconfigured node taints to allow mixed workload scheduling.

title: Batch ETL pipeline processing sluggishness and task timeouts
reported_symptoms: Our nightly Spark ETL jobs are taking three times longer to complete than they did last week. Tasks are timing out when communicating with the shuffle service, but disk and network IO look completely fine.
investigation: Analyzed Spark executor logs and found unexpected garbage collection pauses and thread blocking. Inspected container cgroups and found massive nr_throttled counters ticking up constantly during heavy data transformation stages.
root_cause: A cluster-wide policy update applied tight CPU limits to all batch processing pods, throttling Java virtual machine threads.
resolution: Exempted the Spark worker deployments from the default CPU limit policy and redeployed.

title: Vector DB Deployment Timeout on Image Pull
reported_symptoms: Our milvus deployment is hanging during rolling updates. Pods get stuck in ImagePullBackOff for hours before failing completely.
investigation: Looked into kubelet logs on the affected nodes. Found errors matching 'server returned 429 Too Many Requests: rate limit exceeded'. Confirmed no local cache existed on fresh nodes.
root_cause: The container image download was blocked because anonymous IP-based rate limits were exhausted by surrounding cluster workloads.
resolution: Switched base images to our private cloud registry and set up proper authentication credentials within the deployment manifests.

title: Ray cluster worker node TLS handshake error
reported_symptoms: Worker nodes fail to join the Ray head node. The Raylet logs are flooded with encryption handshake failures and certificate warnings.
investigation: Logged into the Ray head node and checked internal TLS certificates. Executed command 'openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in ray-tls.crt' and found the expiration date was in the past. Verified that secure gRPC communication was completely blocked.
root_cause: The Ray operator generated TLS assets during initial cluster deployment without configuring a renewal mechanism for long-running jobs.
resolution: Rotated the internal TLS credentials using the Ray cluster management CLI and restarted all head and worker node daemons.

title: API Gateway Pods CrashLooping on Startup
reported_symptoms: Our production API gateway pods are restarting constantly. The error message mentions something about image manifest fetch failures.
investigation: Queried events using kubectl get events --field-selector type=Warning. Discovered persistent 'rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull and unpack' with underlying 429 errors.
root_cause: High frequency automated deployments exhausted anonymous pull quotas against the upstream public registry.
resolution: Implemented an internal caching proxy and updated the helm charts to route all image pulls through the authenticated proxy.

title: Embedding generation service connection reset
reported_symptoms: Clients are unable to send batch requests to Triton. The pods are running fine, but any curl test from another pod results in immediate connection refused.
investigation: Verified DNS resolution was working properly for triton-grpc.svc.cluster.local. Ran kubectl get endpoints triton-grpc and confirmed zero active endpoints. Checked pod labels versus service selector and found the service targeted version=v2.1, but the pod labels were updated to version=v2.2 during a recent deploy.
root_cause: Stale service selector version tag left over after an application upgrade.
resolution: Updated the service selector version label to v2.2 to match the active pod fleet.

title: Batch ETL pipeline migration blocked indefinitely
reported_symptoms: Our nightly Spark jobs are failing to reschedule onto new nodes after the recent kernel patch rollout. The old pods won't terminate.
investigation: Examined node conditions and drain logs. Found persistent refusal messages from the API server regarding spark-worker-pdb. The yaml specification showed minAvailable: 100 percent for a single-replica worker group.
root_cause: Percentage-based PDB evaluation equated to zero disruptions allowed since the total replica count was low.
resolution: Modified the PDB resource to use numeric values instead of percentages, unblocking the node drain immediately.

title: API Gateway Pods Restarting Constantly
reported_symptoms: Frontend teams report random disconnects. Pod descriptions show high restart counts with zero error logs.
investigation: Inspected kubelet logs on the worker node. Found multiple entries: Probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503. The app was simply busy compiling routing tables on boot.
root_cause: Aggressive liveness probe settings flagged the container as dead while it was busy processing initial TLS handshakes and route compilation.
resolution: Increased failureThreshold from 3 to 6 and added a startup probe to protect the service during startup.

title: LLM Inference Pods Cycling Continuously
reported_symptoms: Our heavy language model containers keep dropping connections and restarting every three minutes right after initialization. We think it is an out-of-memory error because the nodes have large GPUs attached.
investigation: Checked pod telemetry and observed repeated SIGKILL signals from the runtime. Inspected events via kubectl describe pod llm-node-7b-8ff: Warning Unhealthy: Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500. Container memory usage was actually well below limits at 14GB out of 32GB.
root_cause: The application takes roughly four minutes to load model weights into VRAM, but the liveness probe timeout was configured to kick in after ninety seconds.
resolution: Implemented a dedicated startupProbe with a generous failureThreshold of 30 and increased periodSeconds to 10, giving the weight-loading phase enough time to complete before liveness monitoring takes over.

title: StableDiffusion rendering jobs crashing on high resolution
reported_symptoms: Batch generation jobs for 4K images are throwing mysterious worker loss exceptions.
investigation: Checked pod telemetry and found container memory climbing steadily until hitting the 24Gi boundary. System logs displayed kernel messages: Out of memory: Kill process score 995 or sacrifice child.
root_cause: Unoptimized latent tensor caching exceeded the configured container memory threshold.
resolution: Upgraded memory limits to 48Gi and enabled aggressive garbage collection between batches.

title: Vector DB replication failing post-maintenance
reported_symptoms: Shard sync between our primary and backup vector database pods is throwing timeout errors. We verified DNS resolution works, but synchronization requests drop silently.
investigation: Checked socket connectivity between pods. $ kubectl exec -it milvus-worker-0 -- telnet milvus-worker-1.local 19530. Command hung indefinitely. Inspected active network policies and identified a strict zero-trust baseline policy dropped pod-to-pod traffic within the same namespace.
root_cause: Default-deny isolation policy blocked peer communication across pod selectors without proper allow selectors.
resolution: Applied a tailored NetworkPolicy enabling bidirectional pod communication within the vector database component selector labels.

title: Falcon-40B training stuck at iteration 500
reported_symptoms: Distributed training abruptly stopped making progress. GPU utilization is at zero across all nodes and the job eventually timed out with NCCL watchdog errors.
investigation: Investigated node health using internal tooling. Executed kubectl exec -it <pod> -- python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())'. Checked cluster fabric health and found severe latency degradation on node-f3-n11 due to thermal throttling of the InfiniBand adapter.
root_cause: Thermal throttling on node-f3-n11 caused severe packet delivery delays, causing timeout exceptions across the entire training ring.
resolution: Cordoned and drained node-f3-n11, requested cooling check from facility technicians, and helped the user restart their workload.

title: Real-Time Fraud Detection Service Outage
reported_symptoms: Incoming transaction evaluations are timing out. The primary deployment has zero available replicas running.
investigation: Inspected cluster node conditions. Node app-pool-08 transitioned to Unknown condition. Cloud provider audit logs showed unexpected hypervisor host migration.
root_cause: Underlying hypervisor maintenance live-migrated the virtual machine instance, causing a temporary network bridge disconnect that dropped kubelet heartbeats.
resolution: Waited for the hypervisor migration to complete, verified network interface initialization, and watched Kubernetes automatically transition the node back to Ready.

title: Distributed PyTorch training job failing immediately on startup
reported_symptoms: Training worker nodes drop dead seconds after initialization. We suspect a CUDA driver mismatch on the nodes.
investigation: Inspected pod logs using kubectl logs pytorch-worker-0 --previous. Discovered application error: KeyError: 'MASTER_PORT' not found in os.environ.
root_cause: A recent ConfigMap update removed a required communication parameter needed by the distributed training launcher script.
resolution: Restored the missing key in the mounted ConfigMap and restarted the job successfully.

title: LLM Inference API pods terminating unexpectedly under load
reported_symptoms: Our high-throughput model serving deployment keeps dropping replicas. Requests are timing out and the API gateway returns 502s. We suspect memory leaks in our model weights loading routine.
investigation: Checked cluster status and found pods on node gpu-worker-09 in Evicted state. Ran kubectl describe node gpu-worker-09 and observed DiskPressure true. Inspected kubelet logs which showed EvictionThresholdMet: container garbage collection failed because disk usage exceeded 90 percent.
root_cause: The root volume filled up due to rapid accumulation of heavy HuggingFace model cache files and unpruned container layers.
resolution: Cleaned up unused Docker images and pruned the local cache. Implemented strict ephemeral-storage resource limits in the deployment manifests to prevent recurrence.

title: Batch ETL processing queue blocked
reported_symptoms: Our nightly analytics ETL pipeline is not processing any data. Spark executors remain unassigned.
investigation: Reviewed Kubernetes events using kubectl get events --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp'. Discovered repeated warnings: 'Insufficient cpu'. Cluster capacity was entirely locked up by concurrent developer namespaces.
root_cause: Resource quotas for the customer's namespace were fully exhausted, preventing the creation of new executor pods despite cluster-level idle CPU capacity.
resolution: Increased the namespace CPU hard limit quota and implemented a priority class for time-sensitive batch processing workloads.

title: Real-time fraud detection API returning 504 gateway errors
reported_symptoms: Our payment gateway integration is throwing timeout errors for 5 percent of incoming transactions. The application error tracking tool shows no exceptions thrown by our code.
investigation: Checked ingress controller access logs and confirmed upstream timeouts. Verified that GPU and memory usage were nominal. Queried node-exporter metrics and identified high container cpu throttling ratios across all replicas.
root_cause: An overly restrictive CPU limit was throttling the async event loop during peak transaction traffic spikes.
resolution: Raised the CPU limit parameter in the Helm chart values file and performed a rolling restart.

title: Inference deployment stuck in init state
reported_symptoms: Our high-throughput LLM serving endpoint failed to come up after the latest helm upgrade. All replicas are perpetually stuck and nothing is serving traffic.
investigation: Checked pod status via kubectl. Output showed: 0/12 nodes are available: 3 insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 9 node(s) had untolerated taint. Inspected cluster autoscaler logs and verified node groups were maxed out.
root_cause: Requested 8 A100 GPUs per pod, but available worker nodes only featured 4-GPU topologies or were fully saturated by background batch workloads.
resolution: Scaled down the per-pod GPU requirement to 4 via tensor parallelism adjustments and added two new gpu-compute node pools.

title: Backend API gateway dropping internal microservice calls
reported_symptoms: Clients are getting 504 Gateway Timeouts on auth requests. The auth service pods are running, and CoreDNS resolves their endpoints immediately, but requests fail.
investigation: Traced packet flow using a temporary debug pod. $ kubectl run tmp-debug --rm -it --image=nicolaka/netshoot -- bash. Then ran: nc -z -v auth-service 8081. Connection timed out. Inspected policy objects: Name: default-deny-all. Namespace: production.
root_cause: A newly minted default-deny ingress security baseline blocked requests coming from the gateway ingress controller.
resolution: Created an allowlisting NetworkPolicy permitting the API gateway to communicate with the internal authentication service.

title: Diffusion model training job unable to access checkpoint storage
reported_symptoms: Stable Diffusion training pods are crashing on startup with permission or mount errors. We think the IAM role for the bucket was changed.
investigation: Reviewed pod descriptions: kubectl describe pod sd-trainer-node-5. Discovered repeated error logs: MountVolume.SetUp failed: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = Volume attachment process took longer than 30 seconds.
root_cause: CSI controller pod became unresponsive due to a memory leak, freezing all volume operations cluster-wide.
resolution: Restarted the CSI controller deployment in the kube-system namespace and verified volume attachment success.

title: PyTorch distributed job hangs on gradient sync
reported_symptoms: Batch job failed after 4 hours with a cryptic NCCL error. The logs say 'Watchdog terminating job'. We suspect a deadlock in our custom dataloader pipeline.
investigation: Pulled pod telemetry. kubectl get pods showed running state, but inside containers, CPU utilization was flatlined. Ran ibv_devinfo on worker nodes and found node-a4-n19 had a faulted HCA context throwing driver errors.
root_cause: Host Channel Adapter (HCA) microcode crash on node-a4-n19 halted all RDMA operations, freezing the collective communication ring.
resolution: Cordoned node-a4-n19, performed a hard host reboot to reset the PCIe bus, and verified node health before returning it to the cluster inventory.

title: Model monitoring metrics exporter crashlooping
reported_symptoms: The GPU metrics exporter pod keeps restarting every ten seconds. Grafana shows no data.
investigation: Ran kubectl logs gpu-exporter-899bc-2w1qj --previous. Log output: Error: Invalid metric collection interval 'fast' specified. Must be an integer number of seconds.
root_cause: The user entered a string description instead of an integer for the polling frequency configuration variable.
resolution: Changed the interval parameter value from 'fast' to '15' in the deployment configuration map.

title: Distributed training jobs failing to schedule
reported_symptoms: PyTorchJob controller reports pods cannot be scheduled. We have been waiting for hours and our checkpoint training is halted.
investigation: Ran kubectl describe pod. Found persistent events: FailedScheduling with message '0/40 nodes are available: 40 Insufficient memory'. Node allocatable memory values were entirely consumed by daemonsets.
root_cause: The distributed training configuration requested 256Gi memory per worker pod, exceeding the total physical RAM available on our standard GPU worker node instances.
resolution: Optimized memory requests down to 180Gi and enabled swap configurations on the node template to accommodate peak memory spikes.

title: Vector database cluster pods unable to resolve peer addresses
reported_symptoms: Milvus query nodes are failing health checks and failing to join the cluster ring. Logs show repeated temporary failure in name resolution for data nodes.
investigation: Queried cluster DNS health using nslookup from a debug pod and confirmed intermittent resolution failures. Inspected kube-dns autoscaler configuration and found it was not scaling adequately with node growth.
root_cause: The CoreDNS cluster-proportional-autoscaler formula was set too conservatively, resulting in too few DNS instances for a cluster of this node count.
resolution: Adjusted the autoscaler parameters to maintain a higher ratio of CoreDNS replicas per node and successfully restarted the affected milvus pods.

title: Node maintenance timeout during cluster upgrade for inference nodes
reported_symptoms: Our scheduled node upgrade is totally frozen. The machine is stuck in draining status for over two hours and nothing is migrating.
investigation: Checked drain status using command kubectl drain ip-10-0-44-12. The output showed Warning: ignoring DaemonSet-managed pods and then stalled indefinitely on pod vllm-api-7b89f-k9x2l. Describing the pod revealed it was blocked by a strict policy: eviction was rejected because PodDisruptionBudget vllm-pdb requires minAvailable to be equal to the current replica count.
root_cause: The customer deployed a PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable set to the exact total replica count of two, leaving zero budget for voluntary evictions during maintenance.
resolution: Advised the client to scale their replica deployment to three temporarily, allowing the node drain to proceed, after which they reverted the count.

title: Model monitoring dashboard returning gateway errors
reported_symptoms: Grafana UI loads intermittently and then shows Bad Gateway when trying to query Prometheus metrics from the GPU cluster.
investigation: Checked ingress controller logs, which showed 503 upstream connect errors. Ran kubectl describe service prometheus-svc and discovered <none> under Endpoints. Inspected the Prometheus StatefulSet labels and found app.kubernetes.io/name=prom, whereas the service was selecting app=prometheus.
root_cause: Service selector did not align with standard Helm chart label conventions used in the deployment.
resolution: Applied a patch to the service object to use the correct Helm app.kubernetes.io/name selector.

title: Vision Transformer model crashes with timeout
reported_symptoms: Our ViT training pipeline freezes randomly every few hours. We have to manually kill the pods and restart. It is destroying our experiment velocity.
investigation: Reviewed cluster-level monitoring dashboards. Network throughput on node-e5-n02 dropped to zero while remaining nodes waited indefinitely. syslog output revealed recurrent link-state changes: mlx5_core: Port down.
root_cause: Faulty top-of-rack switch port caused repeated link drops on node-e5-n02, breaking the synchronization barrier during distributed backward passes.
resolution: Shifted the customer pod allocation away from the affected rack, moved node-e5-n02 to maintenance, and guided the team to resume execution.

title: GPU Cluster Node Unresponsive During Model Compilation
reported_symptoms: Compilation job hung for hours. Pods cannot be deleted and kubectl delete pod hangs indefinitely.
investigation: Ran node diagnostics via out-of-band management interface. CPU utilization was pinned at 100 percent with high load averages. Output: uptime - load average: 128.40, 115.20, 104.10.
root_cause: Kernel thread starvation caused by a runaway compilation process locked the system scheduler, rendering the kubelet incapable of reporting health.
resolution: Performed a hard IPMI reset of the node, forced deletion of stuck pods using grace-period set to zero, and verified cluster state normalization.

title: Real-time Fraud Detection Service Crash Loop
reported_symptoms: Our latency-sensitive fraud detection pods are cycling every two minutes in the staging cluster.
investigation: Checked endpoint responsiveness during boot. The service takes 120 seconds to load fraud rules into memory, but liveness checks started at 30 seconds.
root_cause: The liveness probe was misconfigured without considering the time required to deserialize large rule matrices into RAM.
resolution: Configured a startupProbe with a 150-second timeout and adjusted liveness probe execution intervals.

title: Vector database pod deployment timeout
reported_symptoms: Our database migration script failed because the primary index pods never transition out of the pending phase.
investigation: Executed kubectl get pods -A. Observed status Pending on query-node pods. Inspected scheduler metrics confirming zero nodes matched the requested custom node selector label 'accelerator=h100'.
root_cause: The customer specified an outdated node selector label for H100 nodes that had been deprecated during the recent cluster-wide hardware upgrade cycle.
resolution: Updated the deployment manifests with the current node selector labels and successfully rescheduled the vector database pods.

title: Distributed training synchronization stalling across GPU nodes
reported_symptoms: Our multi-node LLM training run froze at step 4500. Nodes are still up in Kubernetes, but NCCL communications are timing out.
