investigation: Checked NCCL debug logs via kubectl logs -n training-ns trainer-worker-0: NCCL WARN Connect/Accept failed: Connection timed out. Verified inter-pod network connectivity with netcat; packet loss detected on the secondary storage network interface.
root_cause: A rogue background storage synchronization job saturated the auxiliary network fabric, causing NCCL heartbeat timeouts between the GPU compute nodes.
resolution: Suspended the heavy storage backup job, drained the affected network queues, and restarted the training run from the latest checkpoint.

title: Vector DB query failures from microservices
reported_symptoms: Search queries from the backend API are failing with upstream connect errors. The database pods are up, but traffic is not reaching them.
investigation: Looked at kube-proxy logs and network policies, finding no drops. Executed kubectl get endpoints milvus-service and confirmed no endpoints were registered. Reviewed the deployment and service manifests side-by-side. The service selector had component=milvus-querynode while the running pods had component=query-node.
root_cause: Divergence in naming conventions for the component selector label.
resolution: Edited the service selector to point to component=query-node so endpoints populated correctly.

title: Stable Diffusion rendering cluster failing to scale
reported_symptoms: Our image generation queue is backing up heavily. The API service is healthy, but backend worker pods tasked with rendering images are not being scheduled by Kubernetes.
investigation: Inspected the pending pods using kubectl get pods --field-status=Pending. Described one of the stuck pods and located the scheduling failure reason: insufficient quota. Verified namespace usage via kubectl describe resourcequota.
root_cause: The ephemeral storage request on the rendering pods pushed the namespace past its total ephemeral storage quota allocation.
resolution: Reduced the per-pod ephemeral storage request value in the Helm chart templates and re-applied the configuration to bring total usage below the quota limit.

title: Computer Vision Inference Failing Intermittently
reported_symptoms: Intermittent HTTP 500 errors on our object detection endpoint. Some requests succeed while others fail instantly.
investigation: Correlated error spikes with specific worker nodes using Grafana dashboards. Logged into worker cv-worker-12 and ran dmesg -T | grep NVRM, uncovering multiple Xid 68 exceptions during heavy batch processing workloads.
root_cause: Processor exception on the accelerator triggered by thermal throttling combined with a transient bus fault.
resolution: Evicted all workloads from the node, cleaned accumulated dust from cooling fans, and reset the PCIe slot configuration in BIOS.

title: Distributed PyTorch training job failing on worker 4
reported_symptoms: Training crashed midway through epoch three with generic exit code 137. The checkpoint writer failed and now worker-4 refuses to schedule new jobs.
investigation: Ran kubectl get pods -A | grep Evicted and spotted the training pod. Described the affected node: output showed Status DiskPressure and Events indicated that the kubelet evicted the pod due to local ephemeral storage exhaustion.
root_cause: Frequent heavy checkpoint writing to the ephemeral container filesystem instead of the mounted persistent volume filled the root disk.
resolution: Pruned dangling Docker volumes, freed up 120GB of disk space, and updated the training job configuration to output checkpoints directly to the shared NFS storage mount.

title: Computer vision pipeline deployment failing image retrieval
reported_symptoms: Our video analytics pods are not starting up after we updated the image repository path in our GitOps repo. Everything is red on our dashboard.
investigation: Checked ArgoCD status and saw degraded state for the cv-app. Ran kubectl describe pod -l app=vision and found ErrImagePull due to a 404 Not Found error from the container registry for repository 'cv/processor-gpu'.
root_cause: The repository name was misspelled during the migration from our legacy registry to the new internal harbor registry.
resolution: Corrected the repository URL typo in the Git repository, synced the ArgoCD application, and verified normal pod startup.

title: Batch ETL Pipeline Failures Due to Node Drop
reported_symptoms: Nightly data processing jobs failed abruptly. Executors on node worker-batch-02 disappeared without writing completion logs.
investigation: Queried Prometheus metrics for node resource saturation. Worker node experienced massive swap thrashing preceding the outage. Output: dmesg - Out of memory: Kill process 1421 (kubelet) score 999.
root_cause: Unbounded memory consumption by local log aggregators starved the kubelet of system resources, triggering node NotReady status.
resolution: Evicted non-essential daemonsets, cordoned the node, adjusted resource limits for system components, and restarted the kubelet service.

title: Model evaluation job failing on startup
reported_symptoms: We launched our weekend evaluation suite and none of the pods are progressing past container creation. The logs are totally empty.
investigation: Ran kubectl get pod eval-job-xyz -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[*].state}' and observed ImagePullBackOff with message: rpc error: code = NotFound. Checked the container registry UI and verified the image was never pushed by the evaluation pipeline script.
root_cause: A syntax error in the evaluation script caused the docker push command to be skipped during execution.
resolution: Fixed the script bug, manually built and pushed the container image, and recreated the Kubernetes job successfully.

title: Vector database ingestion pipeline hanging indefinitely
reported_symptoms: Document indexing jobs are freezing halfway through processing. Workers stay alive but make no progress and eventually fail with gateway timeouts.
investigation: Queried worker pod logs and saw repeated connection reset errors during embedding generation batches. Executed kubectl top pods and noticed moderate CPU usage but zero memory leaks. Traced outgoing calls via Jaeger and discovered embedding-service calls hanging for over 60 seconds.
root_cause: The embedding microservice was bogged down by a heavy upstream batch request from another tenant, severely degrading response times for our workers.
resolution: Applied rate limiting on the embedding service to protect downstream resources and implemented aggressive circuit breaking in the rag-ingest client configuration.

title: Inference Pods Stuck in Terminating State
reported_symptoms: Our high-throughput LLM endpoints are dropping traffic and existing requests are hanging indefinitely. Several pods are stuck in Terminating.
investigation: Checked cluster node health. Node gpu-worker-09 is reporting Status NotReady. Kubelet is unresponsive and systemd shows repeated OOM kills for the daemon. Output: kubectl get nodes - NAME gpu-worker-09 STATUS NotReady.
root_cause: The kubelet process crashed due to kernel memory pressure, causing the control plane to lose node heartbeats.
resolution: Drained the affected node, power-cycled the underlying physical instance, and verified all inference pods rescheduled successfully onto healthy capacity.

title: Batch ETL data processing pods disappearing randomly
reported_symptoms: Our nightly ETL pipelines are aborting with mysterious node lost errors. We thought it might be a kernel panic or an OOM killer event, but memory usage metrics look totally fine.
investigation: Reviewed Kubernetes events for the namespace. Found multiple entries stating Pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the limit. Inspected node: kubectl describe node batch-worker-02 confirmed DiskPressure taint applied by kubelet.
root_cause: Spark shuffle temporary data written to emptyDir volumes overwhelmed the local disk capacity of the node.
resolution: Added explicit ephemeral-storage requests and limits to the Spark worker template and configured automatic log rotation.

title: LLM inference pods stuck restarting continuously post configuration patch
reported_symptoms: Our deep learning inference endpoint keeps throwing CrashLoopBackOff errors across all replicas right after we updated the environment variables for maximum batch size.
investigation: Checked pod status showing restarts. Ran kubectl logs vllm-deployment-7b89f-5z9hx --previous which revealed: ValueError: max_model_len 8192 exceeds hardware capacity for tensor parallelism degree 1.
root_cause: The customer provided an invalid integer for the maximum sequence length that violated underlying GPU memory constraints during application initialization.
resolution: Rolled back the deployment revision to restore the previous valid environment variable set and advised the client on proper parameter sizing.

title: API Gateway backend pods crashing during peak traffic
reported_symptoms: Users are complaining of intermittent connection drops. Pods are getting killed and restarted constantly, throwing SIGKILL errors.
investigation: Checked pod termination reasons via kubectl get pod -o jsonpath. Found reason: Evicted and message: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage. Node df output verified root partition was 100 percent utilized by container logs.
root_cause: Excessive debug-level application logging filled up the node disk, triggering emergency eviction by the kubelet.
resolution: Reduced application log verbosity, purged old log files from /var/log/pods, and established log rotation policies.

title: Web Frontend API Gateway Timeouts
reported_symptoms: External clients are seeing 504 Gateway Timeouts. Kubernetes dashboard shows multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff or Unknown.
investigation: Checked cluster API server event streams. Event log showed NodeNotReady for edge-node-01. Journalctl on the node revealed disk I/O lockups. Output: kernel - EXT4-fs error: block device corruption.
root_cause: Underlying NVMe drive encountered severe hardware degradation, placing the filesystem into read-only mode and halting kubelet state writes.
resolution: Cordoned and drained edge-node-01 immediately. Re-provisioned the ingress pods onto backup edge nodes and decommissioned the faulty drive.

title: ETL batch pipeline unable to reach Redis cache
reported_symptoms: Our overnight ETL pods are timing out during Redis handshakes. DNS lookup is successful, but connections hang. We suspect Redis is overloaded or dead.
investigation: Tested direct transport layer reachability. $ nc -zvw3 redis-master.cache.svc 6379. Resulted in operation timed out. Checked applied policies and found a baseline lockdown policy implemented last evening.
root_cause: A cluster-wide default-deny NetworkPolicy intercepted and discarded all transit packets to the cache subnet.
resolution: Authored and deployed a new NetworkPolicy granting the ETL processing pods egress and ingress access to the Redis cache cluster.

title: Inference API pods failing to initialize following midnight credential rotation
reported_symptoms: Our primary LLM inference endpoints are completely down after the automated maintenance window. New replicas refuse to start up and we see error loops across the cluster.
investigation: Checked pod status and noticed continuous CreateContainerConfigError states. Inspected pod description which revealed: Warning Failed 12m (x4 over 14m) kubelet Error: secret "openai-api-keys-v2" not found.
root_cause: The automated credential rotation pipeline deleted the legacy secret object before updating the target deployment configuration.
resolution: Re-created the missing secret object using the internal secrets vault, which immediately allowed the blocked container runtimes to fetch the required env vars and start successfully.

title: Vector DB Replicas Unreachable After Network Flap
reported_symptoms: We lost quorum on our index cluster. Pods on compute-node-03 show Unknown status and queries are failing with timeout errors.
investigation: Reviewed CNI plugin logs and node heartbeat timers. Node compute-node-03 stopped communicating with the API server. Output: kubectl describe node compute-node-03 - KubeletNotReady NetworkUnavailable.
root_cause: A localized network switch partition severed connectivity between the control plane and this specific rack, halting kubelet updates.
resolution: Collaborated with network operations to reset the top-of-rack switch port. Force-deleted orphaned pods once the node recovered.

title: PyTorch distributed training job failing to launch worker pods
reported_symptoms: We kicked off a large language model pretraining run with sixteen nodes, but only four pods ever started. The training controller keeps logging sync failures without giving a clear reason why the workers are missing.
investigation: Inspected the training job custom resource and queried replica sets. The worker replica set had zero ready pods. Executing kubectl get events -n ml-training revealed multiple FailedCreate warnings stating pods quota exceeded for persistent volume claims.
root_cause: The experiment namespace ran out of its designated storage capacity quota, blocking the creation of scratch storage volumes attached to the training worker pods.
resolution: Cleaned up orphaned checkpoints from previous abandoned runs to reclaim storage, and temporarily bumped the storage request quota for the training namespace.

title: Vector DB index build pods crashing on node 14
reported_symptoms: Vector index building jobs are failing with disk full errors. Our ingestion pipeline is completely stalled and queries are returning incomplete results.
investigation: Queried node conditions: kubectl get nodes revealed DiskPressure on worker-vector-14. Checked disk usage via SSH-based telemetry: df -h showed root partition at 99 percent capacity, largely consumed by old log files and dangling build artifacts.
root_cause: Unbounded log generation from debug builds combined with massive temporary index build files exhausted the node root disk space.
resolution: Flushed stale logs, purged orphaned container layers, and resized the underlying EBS boot volume from 50GB to 150GB.

title: LLM Inference Pods Crash with CUDA Out of Memory and Driver Fault
reported_symptoms: Our vLLM deployment keeps crashing every few minutes. Logs show sudden CUDA driver initialization failures across half our replicas.
investigation: Checked pod descriptions and found node gpu-node-04 showing tainted status. Ran kubectl describe node and noticed NVIDIA device plugin reported 0 available accelerators. Inspected system logs via ssh and found dmesg flooded with Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus errors.
root_cause: Physical PCIe bus error caused the primary accelerator to drop offline unexpectedly.
resolution: Cordoned the affected worker, evicted all active workloads, and initiated a remote baseboard management controller power cycle. Hardware team dispatched for physical seating check.

title: Vector DB Pods Never Registering Endpoints
reported_symptoms: Embeddings search queries are timing out entirely. The replicas are up according to kubectl get pods, yet no endpoints exist under the service.
investigation: Inspected describe output for the coordinator pods. Discovered continuous HTTP 404 errors on the probe path. Snippet: Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404.
root_cause: Readiness probe path was set to /readyz, but the embedded web framework exposed the status endpoint at /api/v1/health.
resolution: Modified the readinessProbe.httpGet.path attribute in the manifests to point to /api/v1/health and performed a rolling restart.

title: Embedding Pipeline Batch Jobs Stuck in Pending State
reported_symptoms: None of our new embedding generation pods are scheduling. They are stuck with Unschedulable: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
investigation: Inspected cluster capacity and found the target node reporting 3 instead of 4 available GPUs to the scheduler. Checked Kubelet logs, observing repeated plugin registration errors. Ran nvidia-smi topo -m to verify link states and found device 2 flagged as faulty by the kernel following an Xid 62 interrupt timeout.
root_cause: Internal firmware panic on GPU 2 leading to an unresponsive state and device plugin quarantine.
resolution: Cordoned the host, performed an automated node drain, and ran an out-of-band firmware reset via IPMI. Verified healthy status before returning to pool.

title: Milvus index build failing on large dataset ingestion
reported_symptoms: Vector database worker pods are dropping off the network whenever we push our nightly embedding batch.
investigation: Ran kubectl logs milvus-worker-559d8-9cltp --previous and saw the process abruptly halted with exit code 137. Node-level dmesg output confirmed kernel invoked oom-killer on the container process due to memory exhaustion.
root_cause: The in-memory IVF index build process required more RAM than the provisioned 32Gi pod ceiling.
resolution: Adjusted the worker resource limits to 64Gi and optimized segment size configurations.

title: Web Backend Deployment Stuck in Pending
reported_symptoms: We pushed a new tag to our web app, but Kubernetes refuses to deploy it. The pods are stuck indefinitely.
investigation: Checked describe pod output showing: 'Warning Failed 3m (x12 over 15m) kubelet Error: ImagePullBackOff'. Traced registry response headers showing rate limit counters depleted.
root_cause: Development teams were pulling large container layers anonymously without rate-limit exemption plans.
resolution: Migrated the container repository to an authenticated enterprise endpoint and updated deployment specs with valid credentials.

title: Batch ETL Worker Pods Failing Endpoint Checks
reported_symptoms: Our nightly GPU-accelerated ETL pipeline is deadlocked. Pods spin up, consume GPU memory for a second, and then Kubernetes starts killing and restarting them endlessly.
investigation: Examined previous pod termination logs. Found SIGKILL signals driven by startup probe failures, cascading into readiness issues. Snippet: Warning Unhealthy Pod status: Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503.
root_cause: The readiness check executed a heavy database connectivity query on every tick, overwhelming the local connection pool and causing self-inflicted timeouts.
resolution: Switched the readiness probe from a dynamic database query endpoint to a lightweight static file check inside the container.

title: Milvus Vector DB GPU Acceleration Lost
reported_symptoms: Vector similarity search latency spiked tenfold. Queries are falling back to CPU mode because CUDA devices are missing.
investigation: Queried Prometheus metrics for cluster hardware health and noticed zero throughput on node vector-gpu-09. Logged into the node and executed nvidia-smi, which returned 'Unknown Error' when communicating with the driver. Reviewed dmesg output and discovered repetitive Xid 31 GPU memory fault logs.
root_cause: Severe memory bus fault on device 0 causing the NVIDIA kernel module to detach the hardware.
resolution: Marked node unschedulable, safely migrated surviving pods to backup nodes, and scheduled a motherboard replacement with the datacenter tech team.

title: Recommendation Engine Model Retraining Failures
reported_symptoms: PyTorch training pods abort immediately upon startup with 'CUDA error: unknown error' messages.
investigation: Ran nvidia-smi on the assigned node and received a driver communication failure notification. Checked system journalctl logs and found persistent Xid 13 graphics engine exceptions preceding driver unresponsiveness.
root_cause: Graphics processing cluster crash caused by unstable voltage regulation to the PCIe riser.
resolution: Cordoned node rec-gpu-05, executed a graceful node drain, and requested onsite technicians reseat the power cables and riser board.

title: LLM fine-tuning job dying midway through epoch two
reported_symptoms: Training keeps halting without error logs in our application layer. The job just disappears from the active queue.
investigation: Inspected cluster event logs via kubectl get events --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp'. Noticed repeated SIGKILL signals from the kernel. Checked cAdvisor metrics confirming RSS memory crossed the 64Gi threshold.
root_cause: Gradient accumulation buffer size was doubled without scaling the Kubernetes pod memory limit accordingly.
resolution: Reverted the batch configuration change and scaled pod memory limits to 96Gi.

title: Vector database instances looping in crash state
reported_symptoms: After pushing our new helm chart values file, none of the query nodes can stay alive. They just restart endlessly.
investigation: Executed kubectl describe pod milvus-query-0 to review termination states. Checked previous container logs and found: yaml: line 42: mapping values are not allowed in this context.
root_cause: Malformed YAML syntax in the custom values override broke the configuration parser during initialization.
resolution: Corrected the indentation error in the customer-supplied helm values file and redeployed the service.

title: Real-time recommendation engine throwing HTTP 504 errors
reported_symptoms: Our recommendation API is returning 504 status codes to the mobile app gateway. Customers see empty recommendations sections.
investigation: Analyzed Prometheus metrics for recsys-api and confirmed request latency p99 jumped from 45ms to 12000ms. Checked Redis cache cluster metrics and observed 100% CPU utilization and memory fragmentation.
root_cause: A corrupted cache key pattern caused a sudden cache stampede, flooding the backing SQL database with concurrent queries and blocking the API workers.
resolution: Flushed the affected Redis cache keys, enabled randomized cache expiration offsets, and restarted the recsys-api deployment pods.

title: Nightly batch ETL pipeline pods failing to spawn
reported_symptoms: Our scheduled data transformation pipeline failed to process last night. Executors are completely missing, and the driver pod has been sitting idle waiting for workers that never materialize.
investigation: Checked SparkApplication status which reported submission failure. Ran kubectl describe ns analytics-batch and saw that the compute resource consumption matched the hard quota limits defined by the cluster administrator.
root_cause: A concurrent reporting batch job had consumed all available CPU units within the shared analytics namespace, leaving zero headroom for the ETL pipeline executors.
resolution: Rescheduled the reporting job to run during off-peak hours and optimized the Spark executor CPU request values to fit within the existing namespace quota bounds.

title: LLM Inference Endpoint Stuck in Pending Readiness State
reported_symptoms: Our heavy GPU inference deployment refuses to shift traffic. Pods say Running for half an hour, but the load balancer reports zero healthy backends.
investigation: Checked pod descriptions and found readiness probe failures on port 8000. Logs showed the app listening on 8080. Snippet: Readiness probe failed: Get http://10.244.1.55:8000/healthz: dial tcp 10.244.1.55:8000: connect: connection refused.
root_cause: The container port definition and the readiness probe target port were mismatched in the latest Helm chart revision.
resolution: Updated the deployment YAML to target port 8080 where the HTTP server actually binds, then applied the change via kubectl.

title: Vector database secure gRPC disconnects
reported_symptoms: Our embedding similarity search service is throwing connection reset errors. The Python client SDK says the SSL peer certificate has expired.
investigation: Inspected TLS assets mounted inside the milvus proxy pods. Ran 'cfssl-certinfo -cert tls.crt' which confirmed the validity period ended three hours ago. Checked cert-manager resources and found an invalid staging issuer reference.
root_cause: An expired self-signed cluster certificate was not rotated because the underlying Secret resource was locked by a manual override tag.
resolution: Removed the conflicting annotation, deleted the stale secret, and forced cert-manager to provision a fresh certificate.

title: ETL batch pipeline pods dropping connection to database
reported_symptoms: Our nightly analytics run is failing halfway through. Database admins report abrupt TCP drops from our Spark workers.
investigation: Queried pod history with kubectl get pod spark-worker-1 -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[*].lastState.terminated}'. Output showed exitCode: 137. Grafana memory dashboard indicated JVM heap usage reached the container boundary.
root_cause: Spark executor memory overhead parameter was set too low for heavy shuffle operations.
resolution: Updated the Helm chart values to allocate more headroom and increased pod memory limits from 16Gi to 32Gi.

title: API Gateway rollout hung on node decommission
reported_symptoms: We initiated a manual node cordoning and draining procedure for host replacement, but the process has been hanging at 50 percent completion for ages.
investigation: Ran kubectl get pdb and noticed web-backend-pdb had allowed disruptions set to 0. Reviewing the object definition confirmed spec.minAvailable matched spec.replicas exactly.
root_cause: The application team locked down the PDB to prevent any traffic drop during updates, which inadvertently blocked infrastructure-level maintenance drains.
resolution: Collaborated with the customer to adjust their PDB minAvailable threshold downward by one, allowing the node drain to finish smoothly.

title: Computer Vision API Service Endpoint Exhaustion
reported_symptoms: Clients are getting 503 Service Unavailable errors from our image segmentation API. Pods show up as running in the dashboard, but traffic isn't reaching them.
investigation: Queried endpoint slices and checked kubelet logs. Snippet: Probe error: invalid port specification: 'http-api'.
root_cause: The engineer referenced a named port in the readiness probe spec, but the container definition declared a numeric port without matching metadata.
resolution: Corrected the port mapping inside the readiness probe configuration to reference the exact containerPort integer directly.

title: StableDiffusion rendering service restart loop
reported_symptoms: Image generation pods are crashing instantly upon deployment. We think the GPU memory is exhausted.
investigation: Checked pod logs with kubectl logs comfyui-deployment-64df8-9qrst --previous. Discovered: TypeError: unsupported operand type for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'.
root_cause: An unset feature flag in the new JSON configuration file caused a null pointer dereference during startup routine checks.
resolution: Provided a valid boolean default for the feature flag in the configuration map and restarted the pods.

title: Batch ETL processing pods failing on volume attachment stage
reported_symptoms: Our overnight data processing pipeline failed entirely. The Spark driver pods cannot initialize because of volume errors. Did AWS/GCP revoke our API credentials?
investigation: Queried cluster events using kubectl get events --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp'. Spotted persistent warnings: FailedMount ... MountVolume.WaitForAttach failed for volume "spark-shuff-vol" : volume is busy on node gpu-node-44.
root_cause: Previous Spark driver job was abruptly terminated, leaving the RWO volume locked by the host operating system kernel.
resolution: Cleared the storage lock by restarting the local CSI plugin on gpu-node-44 and unpublishing the target staging path.

title: Batch ETL processing job API timeout
reported_symptoms: Our scheduled data loader cannot talk to the ingestion gateway service. We suspect a firewall or CNI issue blocking internal cluster traffic.
investigation: Tested internal connectivity using a temporary debug pod and confirmed connection refused on the target port. Inspected the service definition and noticed the selector was set to tier=backend, but the deployed ingestion pods were labeled tier=ingestion-worker. Validated that pods were healthy and ready otherwise.
root_cause: Outdated service selector referencing a deprecated tier label value.
resolution: Corrected the service selector tier value to ingestion-worker to route traffic to the processing pods.

title: Monitoring exporter losing scrape targets
reported_symptoms: Prometheus metrics scrapers are showing target down states for our GPU telemetry exporters. Hostnames resolve through DNS without issues, but HTTP scrapes time out.
investigation: Simulated a scrape manually. $ kubectl exec -it prometheus-server-0 -- wget -qO- http://gpu-metrics-exporter.ml-cluster.svc:9400/metrics. Command hung until timeout. Evaluated network security configurations and located a restrictive policy deployed during compliance audit.
root_cause: An isolation NetworkPolicy blocked scraping traffic because the Prometheus namespace lacked explicit ingress permission.
resolution: Added a NetworkPolicy allowing scraping traffic from the monitoring namespace into the application namespace on port 9400.

title: Inference API returning 502 Bad Gateway after auth integration
reported_symptoms: Our hosted llama-3 endpoint is throwing internal gateway errors for every client payload sent since the deployment window concluded an hour ago.
investigation: Checked ingress controller logs and pod stdout. Observed connection refused errors hitting the upstream worker pool. Executed: kubectl logs deployment/vllm-api -n tenant-alpha. Log output showed: [Errno 111] Connect call failed ('10.244.12.9', 8081). Inspected recent gitops commit and noted the upstream listening port was shifted during the secret injection refactor.
root_cause: Typo in the model server target port environment variable inside the deployment manifest.
resolution: Reverted the port configuration in the helm values file back to 8080 and redeployed.

title: Distributed training jobs failing checkpoint sync
reported_symptoms: Training runs on our multi-node cluster crash immediately upon trying to save the epoch one checkpoint to the shared object store.
investigation: Reviewed worker pod stderr streams. Ran kubectl describe pod train-worker-1. Found error: botocore.exceptions.EndpointConnectionError: Could not connect to the endpoint URL: http://minio.storage.svc.cluster.local:9099/bucket. Verified DNS resolution via busybox nslookup and confirmed the storage service exposes port 9000 instead.
root_cause: Incorrect S3 compatible storage endpoint port defined in the training configuration template.

title: Vector search similarity queries throwing HTTP 500
reported_symptoms: Queries against our embedding database are totally broken right now, returning 500 status codes across the board.
investigation: Queried Prometheus metrics for pod error rates and checked proxy logs. Found recurring exception: grpc._channel._InactiveRpcError: Connect to coordinator failed. Checked helm chart values applied earlier today. Discovered the coordinator hostname had an extra subdomain token appended.
root_cause: Mispelled coordinator service DNS name in the proxy deployment environmental parameters.
resolution: Corrected the DNS string in the values.yaml file and applied the patch via ArgoCD.

title: Batch ETL pipeline job aborting on startup
reported_symptoms: Our nightly analytics batch job fails to start and exits with a cryptic networking stack trace.
investigation: Pulled driver pod logs using kubectl logs spark-driver-pod -n analytics. Noticed: java.net.UnknownHostException: spark-master-svc.internal. Invalid metadata server response. Reviewed the cluster configuration change ticket submitted this morning.
root_cause: Outdated master node hostname specified in the spark defaults configuration map.
resolution: Restored the proper internal master hostname in the configmap and triggered a job retry.

title: Web backend unable to fetch user session cache
reported_symptoms: Users are being logged out instantly and API calls fail with redis timeout exceptions after the latest backend release.
investigation: Inspected application pods using kubectl top and logs. Traced the connection string: redis://:***@redis-master.cache.svc:6389/0. Tested connectivity from an ephemeral debug pod and found port closed. Correct port is 6379.
root_cause: Incorrect Redis port specified in the application deployment environment secrets.
resolution: Patched the secret resource with the correct port number and rolled out the deployment.

title: Model monitoring metrics ingestion failing
reported_symptoms: Grafana dashboards show zero data points for GPU utilization metrics since the monitoring agent update.
investigation: Checked adapter logs and found connection timeouts hitting the metrics exporter endpoint. Executed: curl http://dcgm-exporter.monitoring.svc:9400/metrics and received connection reset. Inspected the scrape config and found an incorrect scheme and port combination.
root_cause: Misconfigured scrape endpoint port and protocol schema in the Prometheus operator service monitor.
resolution: Fixed the service monitor YAML definition and forced Prometheus to reload its configuration.

title: Feature store API throwing serialization errors
reported_symptoms: Online feature retrieval requests are failing for all client applications, returning bad request responses.
investigation: Analyzed container logs and identified a failure connecting to the offline registry store. Log excerpt: sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.OperationalError) connection to server at postgresql-registry.db.svc, port 5433 failed: Connection refused. Checked Postgres deployment and verified it listens on standard port 5432.
root_cause: Wrong database port parameter defined in the feature store yaml configuration.
resolution: Updated the database port to 5432 in the global config secret and restarted pods.
